title: Fix athena land --pr rerun after merge; record merge-commit landing
summary: Make `athena land --pr` fetch the merged commit before fingerprinting it. On a rerun with an existing PR link, check the host for the merge before requiring the landed commit on the local branch. Record merge commits as the PR landing shape in the design doc and a new decisions.md entry. Tests cover fixes (1) and (2).

defaults_applied.how: All changes are Rust code and tests, plus markdown docs.
New tests for fixes (1) and (2); cargo test and clippy must pass.
The decision entry cites the PR #39 squash ancestry break and the simulated two-merge-commit `athena check --history` run with 0 violations.
One focused change to the land --pr path and its docs.
The verifier runs cargo test for the new tests.
Docs and the decision entry are written for an outside reader.

assumptions: Fix (1) goes in `GitContent::fingerprint_of` (crates/athena-core/src/pr.rs). It runs `git fetch origin <sha>` when the commit is not present locally, using a new Git method in athena-git.

Fix (2) goes in `Athena::land_pr`: when a stored PR link exists and `landed_commit` fails, the code still runs the host merge check. The head and replace flow need the landed commit. A job that is neither landed locally nor merged on the host keeps the 'not landed on this branch' error.
Once the host confirms the merge and the fingerprint matches, the job reports as landed, even with the landed commit off the current branch.

The design doc is docs/design/native-pr-landing.md, with a short note in docs/design/athena-v0.md section 7.3 if it describes the squash shape for PRs. The decision goes in a new entry D87 in docs/decisions.md.
Tests use the existing fakes in gh.rs and pr.rs, plus a real-git test for the fetch if the athena-git test helpers support a second repository.
No change to the merge request itself: `merge_method` is already `merge`.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test shows that when the merged commit is absent from the local object store but present on the remote, the merged-content check fetches it and returns the fingerprint instead of failing with 'not a tree object'. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.

A test shows that `land_pr` with an existing open PR link, a host that reports the PR merged, and a landed commit not reachable from the local head confirms the landing and does not return 'not landed on this branch'. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
A test shows that with no stored link and no landed commit on the branch, `land_pr` still errors with 'not landed on this branch'. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
`cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`, and `cargo fmt --check` all pass.
docs/design/native-pr-landing.md states that merge commits are the landing shape for pull requests, and that squash merges break ancestry.

docs/decisions.md has a new entry after D86 that records merge commits as the PR landing shape. It cites the #39 squash conflict and the simulated two-merge-commit history passing `athena check --history` with 0 violations.
The fetch uses the existing Git wrapper and does not move any local branch or ref other than fetching the object.

out_of_scope: Changing the merge method or the `merge_via_rest` setting
Changing the history check or the gate's landing rules
Exempting any squash commit from the history check
departures: Slightly higher cost and time than the reference: the change spans two crates, needs a real-git fetch test, and needs two docs edits.
